pycode_kg

pycode_kg: A tool to build a searchable knowledge graph from Python repositories.

Pure AST extraction → SQLite (authoritative) → sqlite-vec (semantic index).

Public API

Primary entry point::

from pycode_kg import PyCodeKG

kg = PyCodeKG(repo_root, db_path)
stats = kg.build(wipe=True)
result = kg.query("database connection setup")
pack = kg.pack("configuration loading")
pack.save("context.md")

Individual layers::

from pycode_kg import CodeGraph, GraphStore, SemanticIndex

Result types::

from pycode_kg import BuildStats, QueryResult, SnippetPack, Snippet

Low-level primitives (v0 contract, locked)::

from pycode_kg import Node, Edge

KGModule SDK (build new domain KGs)::

from pycode_kg import KGModule, KGExtractor, PyCodeKGExtractor, NodeSpec, EdgeSpec

class CodeGraph: 
 22class CodeGraph:
 23    """
 24    Pure, deterministic AST extraction from a Python repository.
 25
 26    Wraps the low-level ``extract_repo`` function with a cached,
 27    object-oriented interface.  No side effects; calling :meth:`extract`
 28    twice on the same root returns the same result.
 29
 30    Example::
 31
 32        graph = CodeGraph("/path/to/repo")
 33        graph.extract()
 34        print(f"{len(graph.nodes)} nodes, {len(graph.edges)} edges")
 35
 36    :param repo_root: Path to the repository root directory.
 37    """
 38
 39    def __init__(
 40        self,
 41        repo_root: str | Path,
 42        include: set[str] | None = None,
 43        exclude: set[str] | None = None,
 44    ) -> None:
 45        """Initialise the graph for a given repository root.
 46
 47        :param repo_root: Path to the repository root directory.
 48        :param include: Set of top-level directory names to include in extraction.
 49                       When non-empty, only these directories are indexed.
 50                       When empty/None, all directories are indexed.
 51        :param exclude: Set of directory names to prune at every walk depth
 52                       (e.g., ``{"tests", "benchmarks"}``).
 53        """
 54        self.repo_root: Path = Path(repo_root).resolve()
 55        self.include: set[str] = include or set()
 56        self.exclude: set[str] = exclude or set()
 57        self._nodes: list[Node] | None = None
 58        self._edges: list[Edge] | None = None
 59
 60    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 61    # Public API
 62    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 63
 64    def extract(self, *, force: bool = False) -> CodeGraph:
 65        """
 66        Run AST extraction (cached after first call).
 67
 68        :param force: Re-extract even if already cached.
 69        :return: self (for chaining)
 70        """
 71        if self._nodes is None or force:
 72            self._nodes, self._edges = extract_repo(
 73                self.repo_root, include=self.include, exclude=self.exclude
 74            )
 75        return self
 76
 77    @property
 78    def nodes(self) -> list[Node]:
 79        """Extracted nodes (calls :meth:`extract` if needed)."""
 80        if self._nodes is None:
 81            self.extract()
 82        assert self._nodes is not None
 83        return self._nodes
 84
 85    @property
 86    def edges(self) -> list[Edge]:
 87        """Extracted edges (calls :meth:`extract` if needed)."""
 88        if self._edges is None:
 89            self.extract()
 90        assert self._edges is not None
 91        return self._edges
 92
 93    def result(self) -> tuple[list[Node], list[Edge]]:
 94        """Return the extracted nodes and edges as a tuple.
 95
 96        :return: ``(nodes, edges)`` tuple, triggering extraction if not yet done.
 97        """
 98        return self.nodes, self.edges
 99
100    def stats(self) -> dict:
101        """
102        Return a summary of extracted nodes and edges by kind/relation.
103
104        :return: dict with ``node_counts``, ``edge_counts``, ``total_nodes``,
105                 ``total_edges``.
106        """
107        node_counts: Counter = Counter(n.kind for n in self.nodes)
108        edge_counts: Counter = Counter(e.rel for e in self.edges)
109        return {
110            "repo_root": str(self.repo_root),
111            "total_nodes": len(self.nodes),
112            "total_edges": len(self.edges),
113            "node_counts": dict(node_counts),
114            "edge_counts": dict(edge_counts),
115        }
116
117    def __repr__(self) -> str:
118        """Return a developer-readable representation of this CodeGraph.
119
120        :return: String including repo root, and node/edge counts if already extracted.
121        """
122        extracted = self._nodes is not None
123        if extracted:
124            return (
125                f"CodeGraph(repo_root={self.repo_root!r}, "
126                f"nodes={len(self._nodes)}, edges={len(self._edges)})"  # ty: ignore[invalid-argument-type]
127            )
128        return f"CodeGraph(repo_root={self.repo_root!r}, not yet extracted)"

Example::

graph = CodeGraph("/path/to/repo")
graph.extract()
print(f"{len(graph.nodes)} nodes, {len(graph.edges)} edges")

class GraphStore: 
106class GraphStore:
107    """SQLite-backed authoritative store for a knowledge graph.
108
109    Manages the ``nodes`` and ``edges`` tables and provides graph traversal
110    primitives consumed by the query layer.
111
112    :param db_path: Path to the SQLite database file (created if absent).
113    """
114
115    def __init__(self, db_path: str | Path) -> None:
116        self.db_path = Path(db_path)
117        self._con: sqlite3.Connection | None = None
118
119    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
120    # Connection management
121    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
122
123    @property
124    def con(self) -> sqlite3.Connection:
125        """Lazy SQLite connection (created on first access)."""
126        if self._con is None:
127            self.db_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
128            self._con = sqlite3.connect(
129                str(self.db_path),
130                check_same_thread=False,
131            )
132            self._con.executescript(_SCHEMA_SQL)
133        return self._con
134
135    def close(self) -> None:
136        """Close the underlying SQLite connection."""
137        if self._con is not None:
138            self._con.close()
139            self._con = None
140
141    def __enter__(self) -> GraphStore:
142        return self
143
144    def __exit__(self, *_: object) -> None:
145        self.close()
146
147    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
148    # Write
149    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
150
151    def clear(self) -> None:
152        """Delete all nodes and edges."""
153        self.con.execute("DELETE FROM edges;")
154        self.con.execute("DELETE FROM nodes;")
155        self.con.commit()
156
157    def write(
158        self,
159        nodes: Sequence[NodeSpec],
160        edges: Sequence[EdgeSpec],
161        *,
162        wipe: bool = False,
163    ) -> None:
164        """Persist a complete graph to SQLite.
165
166        :param nodes: NodeSpec list from a :class:`~kg_utils.types.KGExtractor`.
167        :param edges: EdgeSpec list from a :class:`~kg_utils.types.KGExtractor`.
168        :param wipe: If ``True``, clear existing data before writing.
169        """
170        if wipe:
171            self.clear()
172        self._upsert_nodes(nodes)
173        self._upsert_edges(edges)
174
175    def _upsert_nodes(self, nodes: Iterable[NodeSpec]) -> None:
176        rows = [
177            (
178                n.node_id,
179                n.kind,
180                n.name,
181                n.qualname,
182                n.source_path,
183                n.lineno,
184                n.end_lineno,
185                n.docstring,
186            )
187            for n in nodes
188        ]
189        self.con.executemany(
190            """
191            INSERT INTO nodes
192              (id, kind, name, qualname, module_path, lineno, end_lineno, docstring)
193            VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
194            ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET
195              kind=excluded.kind,
196              name=excluded.name,
197              qualname=excluded.qualname,
198              module_path=excluded.module_path,
199              lineno=excluded.lineno,
200              end_lineno=excluded.end_lineno,
201              docstring=excluded.docstring
202            """,
203            rows,
204        )
205        self.con.commit()
206
207    def _upsert_edges(self, edges: Iterable[EdgeSpec]) -> None:
208        rows = [
209            (
210                e.source_id,
211                e.relation,
212                e.target_id,
213                (json.dumps(e.metadata, ensure_ascii=False) if e.metadata else None),
214            )
215            for e in edges
216        ]
217        self.con.executemany(
218            """
219            INSERT INTO edges (src, rel, dst, evidence)
220            VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)
221            ON CONFLICT(src, rel, dst) DO UPDATE SET
222              evidence=excluded.evidence
223            """,
224            rows,
225        )
226        self.con.commit()
227
228    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
229    # Read — single node
230    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
231
232    def node(self, node_id: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
233        """Fetch a single node by id.
234
235        :param node_id: Stable node identifier.
236        :return: Node dict or ``None`` if not found.
237        """
238        row = self.con.execute(
239            """
240            SELECT id, kind, name, qualname, module_path, lineno, end_lineno, docstring
241            FROM nodes WHERE id = ?
242            """,
243            (node_id,),
244        ).fetchone()
245        return _row_to_node(row) if row else None
246
247    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
248    # Read — filtered node lists
249    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
250
251    def query_nodes(
252        self,
253        *,
254        kinds: Sequence[str] | None = None,
255        module: str | None = None,
256    ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
257        """Return nodes matching optional filters.
258
259        :param kinds: Restrict to these node kinds.
260        :param module: Restrict to nodes in this module path (exact match).
261        :return: List of node dicts.
262        """
263        clauses: list[str] = []
264        params: list[object] = []
265
266        if kinds:
267            placeholders = ",".join("?" for _ in kinds)
268            clauses.append(f"kind IN ({placeholders})")
269            params.extend(kinds)
270
271        if module is not None:
272            clauses.append("module_path = ?")
273            params.append(module)
274
275        where = f"WHERE {' AND '.join(clauses)}" if clauses else ""
276        rows = self.con.execute(
277            f"""
278            SELECT id, kind, name, qualname, module_path, lineno, end_lineno, docstring
279            FROM nodes {where}
280            ORDER BY module_path, lineno
281            """,
282            params,
283        ).fetchall()
284        return [_row_to_node(r) for r in rows]
285
286    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
287    # Read — edges
288    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
289
290    def edges_within(self, node_ids: set[str]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
291        """Return all edges where both src and dst are in *node_ids*.
292
293        :param node_ids: Set of node IDs to restrict to.
294        :return: List of edge dicts.
295        """
296        if not node_ids:
297            return []
298
299        self.con.execute("DROP TABLE IF EXISTS _tmp_ids;")
300        self.con.execute("CREATE TEMP TABLE _tmp_ids (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY);")
301        self.con.executemany("INSERT INTO _tmp_ids (id) VALUES (?)", [(i,) for i in node_ids])
302        rows = self.con.execute(
303            """
304            SELECT e.src, e.rel, e.dst, e.evidence
305            FROM edges e
306            JOIN _tmp_ids s ON s.id = e.src
307            JOIN _tmp_ids d ON d.id = e.dst
308            """
309        ).fetchall()
310        return [{"src": r[0], "rel": r[1], "dst": r[2], "evidence": r[3]} for r in rows]
311
312    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
313    # Graph traversal
314    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
315
316    def expand(
317        self,
318        seed_ids: set[str],
319        *,
320        hop: int = 1,
321        rels: tuple[str, ...] = DEFAULT_RELS,
322    ) -> dict[str, ProvMeta]:
323        """Expand the graph from *seed_ids* up to *hop* hops.
324
325        :param seed_ids: Starting node IDs (hop 0).
326        :param hop: Maximum number of hops to traverse.
327        :param rels: Edge relation types to follow.
328        :return: ``{node_id: ProvMeta}`` for all reachable nodes.
329        """
330        rels = tuple(rels)
331        meta: dict[str, ProvMeta] = {sid: ProvMeta(best_hop=0, via_seed=sid) for sid in seed_ids}
332        frontier: set[str] = set(seed_ids)
333
334        for h in range(1, hop + 1):
335            nxt: set[str] = set()
336            for nid in frontier:
337                rows = self.con.execute(
338                    f"""
339                    SELECT src, dst FROM edges
340                    WHERE (src = ? OR dst = ?)
341                      AND rel IN ({",".join("?" for _ in rels)})
342                    """,
343                    (nid, nid, *rels),
344                ).fetchall()
345                for src, dst in rows:
346                    for cand in (src, dst):
347                        if cand not in meta:
348                            meta[cand] = ProvMeta(best_hop=h, via_seed=meta[nid].via_seed)
349                            nxt.add(cand)
350                        elif h < meta[cand].best_hop:
351                            meta[cand] = ProvMeta(best_hop=h, via_seed=meta[nid].via_seed)
352                            nxt.add(cand)
353            frontier = nxt
354
355        return meta
356
357    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
358    # Symbol resolution (relevant for code KGs with stub nodes)
359    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
360
361    def resolve_symbols(self) -> int:
362        """Add RESOLVES_TO edges from ``sym:`` stub nodes to their definitions.
363
364        Matches stubs to first-party definitions by name (and optionally by
365        fully-qualified dotted name).  Idempotent — duplicate edges are
366        silently ignored.
367
368        :return: Number of new RESOLVES_TO edges written.
369        """
370        sym_rows = self.con.execute(
371            "SELECT id, name, qualname FROM nodes WHERE kind = 'symbol'"
372        ).fetchall()
373
374        def_rows = self.con.execute(
375            """
376            SELECT id, kind, name, qualname, module_path
377            FROM nodes
378            WHERE kind != 'symbol' AND name IS NOT NULL
379            """
380        ).fetchall()
381
382        name_to_defs: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
383        dotted_to_defs: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
384        for def_id, def_kind, def_name, def_qualname, def_module_path in def_rows:
385            name_to_defs.setdefault(def_name, []).append(def_id)
386
387            module_dotted_variants = _module_to_dotted_variants(def_module_path)
388            if def_kind == "module":
389                for module_dotted in module_dotted_variants:
390                    dotted_to_defs.setdefault(module_dotted, []).append(def_id)
391            elif module_dotted_variants and def_qualname:
392                for module_dotted in module_dotted_variants:
393                    dotted_key = f"{module_dotted}.{def_qualname}"
394                    dotted_to_defs.setdefault(dotted_key, []).append(def_id)
395
396        edges: list[tuple[str, str, str, str]] = []
397        for sym_id, sym_name, sym_qualname in sym_rows:
398            if not sym_name:
399                continue
400
401            candidates: list[str] = []
402            mode = "name_fallback"
403            confidence = "medium"
404
405            if sym_qualname and "." in sym_qualname:
406                exact = dotted_to_defs.get(sym_qualname, [])
407                if exact:
408                    candidates = exact
409                    mode = "exact_qualname"
410                    confidence = "high"
411
412            if not candidates:
413                candidates = name_to_defs.get(sym_name, [])
414                if len(candidates) > 1:
415                    mode = "name_fallback_ambiguous"
416                    confidence = "low"
417
418            for def_id in candidates:
419                evidence: dict[str, Any] = {
420                    "resolution_mode": mode,
421                    "confidence": confidence,
422                    "symbol": sym_id,
423                }
424                if mode == "name_fallback_ambiguous":
425                    evidence["candidate_count"] = len(candidates)
426                edges.append(
427                    (
428                        sym_id,
429                        "RESOLVES_TO",
430                        def_id,
431                        json.dumps(evidence, ensure_ascii=False),
432                    )
433                )
434
435        if edges:
436            self.con.executemany(
437                """
438                INSERT INTO edges (src, rel, dst, evidence)
439                VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)
440                ON CONFLICT(src, rel, dst) DO UPDATE SET
441                  evidence=excluded.evidence
442                """,
443                edges,
444            )
445            self.con.commit()
446
447        return len(edges)
448
449    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
450    # Caller lookup (fan-in)
451    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
452
453    def callers_of(self, node_id: str, *, rel: str = "CALLS") -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
454        """Return all nodes that have a *rel* edge pointing at *node_id*.
455
456        Two-phase lookup:
457        1. Direct: ``edges WHERE dst = node_id AND rel = rel``
458        2. Indirect: find ``sym:`` stubs with RESOLVES_TO edges to *node_id*
459           and collect their incoming *rel* edges.
460
461        :param node_id: Target node identifier.
462        :param rel: Relation type to invert (default ``"CALLS"``).
463        :return: List of caller node dicts, deduplicated.
464        """
465        direct = self.con.execute(
466            "SELECT src, evidence FROM edges WHERE dst = ? AND rel = ?",
467            (node_id, rel),
468        ).fetchall()
469
470        stubs = self.con.execute(
471            "SELECT src FROM edges WHERE dst = ? AND rel = 'RESOLVES_TO'",
472            (node_id,),
473        ).fetchall()
474
475        stub_callers: list[tuple[str, str | None, str]] = []
476        for (stub_id,) in stubs:
477            rows = self.con.execute(
478                "SELECT src, evidence FROM edges WHERE dst = ? AND rel = ?",
479                (stub_id, rel),
480            ).fetchall()
481            for src_id, evidence in rows:
482                stub_callers.append((src_id, evidence, stub_id))
483
484        seen: set[str] = set()
485        result: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
486        for caller_id, evidence in direct:
487            if caller_id in seen:
488                continue
489            seen.add(caller_id)
490            n = self.node(caller_id)
491            if n:
492                lineno = _parse_call_site_lineno(evidence)
493                if lineno is not None:
494                    n = {**n, "call_site_lineno": lineno}
495                result.append(n)
496
497        for caller_id, evidence, _stub_id in stub_callers:
498            if caller_id in seen:
499                continue
500            if not self._is_compatible_stub_caller(caller_id, evidence, node_id):
501                continue
502            seen.add(caller_id)
503            n = self.node(caller_id)
504            if n:
505                lineno = _parse_call_site_lineno(evidence)
506                if lineno is not None:
507                    n = {**n, "call_site_lineno": lineno}
508                result.append(n)
509
510        return result
511
512    def _is_compatible_stub_caller(
513        self, caller_id: str, evidence: str | None, target_node_id: str
514    ) -> bool:
515        """Validate a stub-resolved caller against import hints from its module.
516
517        :param caller_id: Caller node ID from an incoming CALLS edge.
518        :param evidence: JSON-encoded edge evidence from the CALLS edge.
519        :param target_node_id: Target node currently being reverse-resolved.
520        :return: ``True`` if caller is compatible with target resolution.
521        """
522        if not evidence:
523            return True
524        try:
525            ev = json.loads(evidence)
526        except (TypeError, json.JSONDecodeError):
527            return True
528
529        expr = ev.get("expr")
530        if not isinstance(expr, str) or not expr:
531            return True
532
533        short_name = expr.split(".")[-1]
534        caller_node = self.node(caller_id)
535        if not caller_node:
536            return True
537
538        module_path = caller_node.get("module_path")
539        if not module_path:
540            return True
541
542        # Generic: find the module node by kind+module_path (no ID prefix assumptions)
543        module_row = self.con.execute(
544            "SELECT id FROM nodes WHERE kind = 'module' AND module_path = ? LIMIT 1",
545            (module_path,),
546        ).fetchone()
547        if not module_row:
548            return True
549
550        module_id = module_row[0]
551        import_rows = self.con.execute(
552            "SELECT dst FROM edges WHERE src = ? AND rel = 'IMPORTS'",
553            (module_id,),
554        ).fetchall()
555
556        matching_import_symbols = [
557            sym_id
558            for (sym_id,) in import_rows
559            if sym_id.startswith("sym:") and sym_id.split(".")[-1] == short_name
560        ]
561        if not matching_import_symbols:
562            return True
563
564        for sym_id in matching_import_symbols:
565            hit = self.con.execute(
566                "SELECT 1 FROM edges WHERE src = ? AND rel = 'RESOLVES_TO' AND dst = ? LIMIT 1",
567                (sym_id, target_node_id),
568            ).fetchone()
569            if hit:
570                return True
571        return False
572
573    def edges_from(
574        self, node_id: str, *, rel: str = "CALLS", limit: int | None = None
575    ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
576        """Return all edges originating from *node_id* with the given relation type.
577
578        :param node_id: Source node identifier.
579        :param rel: Relation type to match (default ``"CALLS"``).
580        :param limit: Maximum number of edges to return (``None`` for unlimited).
581        :return: List of edge dicts with keys ``src``, ``rel``, ``dst``, ``evidence``.
582        """
583        query = "SELECT src, rel, dst, evidence FROM edges WHERE src = ? AND rel = ?"
584        params: list[object] = [node_id, rel]
585        if limit is not None:
586            query += " LIMIT ?"
587            params.append(limit)
588        rows = self.con.execute(query, params).fetchall()
589        return [{"src": r[0], "rel": r[1], "dst": r[2], "evidence": r[3]} for r in rows]
590
591    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
592    # Stats
593    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
594
595    def stats(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
596        """Return node and edge counts by kind/relation, plus domain-specific metrics.
597
598        :return: dict with ``total_nodes``, ``meaningful_nodes``, ``total_edges``,
599                 ``node_counts``, ``edge_counts``, ``docstring_coverage``,
600                 ``snapshot_count``.
601        """
602        node_rows = self.con.execute("SELECT kind, COUNT(*) FROM nodes GROUP BY kind").fetchall()
603        edge_rows = self.con.execute("SELECT rel, COUNT(*) FROM edges GROUP BY rel").fetchall()
604        total_nodes = self.con.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM nodes").fetchone()[0]
605        total_edges = self.con.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM edges").fetchone()[0]
606
607        node_counts: dict[str, int] = {r[0]: r[1] for r in node_rows}
608        symbol_count = node_counts.get("symbol", 0)
609
610        fn_count = node_counts.get("function", 0)
611        method_count = node_counts.get("method", 0)
612        fn_method_total = fn_count + method_count
613        with_doc = self.con.execute(
614            "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM nodes"
615            " WHERE kind IN ('function','method')"
616            " AND docstring IS NOT NULL AND docstring != ''"
617        ).fetchone()[0]
618
619        snapshot_count = 0
620        manifest_path = self.db_path.parent / "snapshots" / "manifest.json"
621        if manifest_path.exists():
622            try:
623                manifest = json.loads(manifest_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
624                snapshot_count = len(manifest.get("snapshots", []))
625            except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError):
626                pass
627
628        return {
629            "db_path": str(self.db_path),
630            "total_nodes": total_nodes,
631            "meaningful_nodes": total_nodes - symbol_count,
632            "total_edges": total_edges,
633            "node_counts": node_counts,
634            "edge_counts": {r[0]: r[1] for r in edge_rows},
635            "module_count": node_counts.get("module", 0),
636            "class_count": node_counts.get("class", 0),
637            "function_count": fn_count,
638            "method_count": method_count,
639            "docstring_coverage": round(with_doc / fn_method_total, 3) if fn_method_total else 0.0,
640            "snapshot_count": snapshot_count,
641        }
642
643    def __repr__(self) -> str:
644        return f"GraphStore(db_path={self.db_path!r})"

def query_nodes( self, *, kinds: Sequence[str] | None = None, module: str | None = None) -> list[dict[str, typing.Any]]: 
251    def query_nodes(
252        self,
253        *,
254        kinds: Sequence[str] | None = None,
255        module: str | None = None,
256    ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
257        """Return nodes matching optional filters.
258
259        :param kinds: Restrict to these node kinds.
260        :param module: Restrict to nodes in this module path (exact match).
261        :return: List of node dicts.
262        """
263        clauses: list[str] = []
264        params: list[object] = []
265
266        if kinds:
267            placeholders = ",".join("?" for _ in kinds)
268            clauses.append(f"kind IN ({placeholders})")
269            params.extend(kinds)
270
271        if module is not None:
272            clauses.append("module_path = ?")
273            params.append(module)
274
275        where = f"WHERE {' AND '.join(clauses)}" if clauses else ""
276        rows = self.con.execute(
277            f"""
278            SELECT id, kind, name, qualname, module_path, lineno, end_lineno, docstring
279            FROM nodes {where}
280            ORDER BY module_path, lineno
281            """,
282            params,
283        ).fetchall()
284        return [_row_to_node(r) for r in rows]

def edges_within(self, node_ids: set[str]) -> list[dict[str, typing.Any]]: 
290    def edges_within(self, node_ids: set[str]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
291        """Return all edges where both src and dst are in *node_ids*.
292
293        :param node_ids: Set of node IDs to restrict to.
294        :return: List of edge dicts.
295        """
296        if not node_ids:
297            return []
298
299        self.con.execute("DROP TABLE IF EXISTS _tmp_ids;")
300        self.con.execute("CREATE TEMP TABLE _tmp_ids (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY);")
301        self.con.executemany("INSERT INTO _tmp_ids (id) VALUES (?)", [(i,) for i in node_ids])
302        rows = self.con.execute(
303            """
304            SELECT e.src, e.rel, e.dst, e.evidence
305            FROM edges e
306            JOIN _tmp_ids s ON s.id = e.src
307            JOIN _tmp_ids d ON d.id = e.dst
308            """
309        ).fetchall()
310        return [{"src": r[0], "rel": r[1], "dst": r[2], "evidence": r[3]} for r in rows]

def expand( self, seed_ids: set[str], *, hop: int = 1, rels: tuple[str, ...] = ('CONTAINS', 'CALLS', 'IMPORTS', 'INHERITS')) -> dict[str, kg_utils.store.ProvMeta]: 
316    def expand(
317        self,
318        seed_ids: set[str],
319        *,
320        hop: int = 1,
321        rels: tuple[str, ...] = DEFAULT_RELS,
322    ) -> dict[str, ProvMeta]:
323        """Expand the graph from *seed_ids* up to *hop* hops.
324
325        :param seed_ids: Starting node IDs (hop 0).
326        :param hop: Maximum number of hops to traverse.
327        :param rels: Edge relation types to follow.
328        :return: ``{node_id: ProvMeta}`` for all reachable nodes.
329        """
330        rels = tuple(rels)
331        meta: dict[str, ProvMeta] = {sid: ProvMeta(best_hop=0, via_seed=sid) for sid in seed_ids}
332        frontier: set[str] = set(seed_ids)
333
334        for h in range(1, hop + 1):
335            nxt: set[str] = set()
336            for nid in frontier:
337                rows = self.con.execute(
338                    f"""
339                    SELECT src, dst FROM edges
340                    WHERE (src = ? OR dst = ?)
341                      AND rel IN ({",".join("?" for _ in rels)})
342                    """,
343                    (nid, nid, *rels),
344                ).fetchall()
345                for src, dst in rows:
346                    for cand in (src, dst):
347                        if cand not in meta:
348                            meta[cand] = ProvMeta(best_hop=h, via_seed=meta[nid].via_seed)
349                            nxt.add(cand)
350                        elif h < meta[cand].best_hop:
351                            meta[cand] = ProvMeta(best_hop=h, via_seed=meta[nid].via_seed)
352                            nxt.add(cand)
353            frontier = nxt
354
355        return meta

def callers_of(self, node_id: str, *, rel: str = 'CALLS') -> list[dict[str, typing.Any]]: 
453    def callers_of(self, node_id: str, *, rel: str = "CALLS") -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
454        """Return all nodes that have a *rel* edge pointing at *node_id*.
455
456        Two-phase lookup:
457        1. Direct: ``edges WHERE dst = node_id AND rel = rel``
458        2. Indirect: find ``sym:`` stubs with RESOLVES_TO edges to *node_id*
459           and collect their incoming *rel* edges.
460
461        :param node_id: Target node identifier.
462        :param rel: Relation type to invert (default ``"CALLS"``).
463        :return: List of caller node dicts, deduplicated.
464        """
465        direct = self.con.execute(
466            "SELECT src, evidence FROM edges WHERE dst = ? AND rel = ?",
467            (node_id, rel),
468        ).fetchall()
469
470        stubs = self.con.execute(
471            "SELECT src FROM edges WHERE dst = ? AND rel = 'RESOLVES_TO'",
472            (node_id,),
473        ).fetchall()
474
475        stub_callers: list[tuple[str, str | None, str]] = []
476        for (stub_id,) in stubs:
477            rows = self.con.execute(
478                "SELECT src, evidence FROM edges WHERE dst = ? AND rel = ?",
479                (stub_id, rel),
480            ).fetchall()
481            for src_id, evidence in rows:
482                stub_callers.append((src_id, evidence, stub_id))
483
484        seen: set[str] = set()
485        result: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
486        for caller_id, evidence in direct:
487            if caller_id in seen:
488                continue
489            seen.add(caller_id)
490            n = self.node(caller_id)
491            if n:
492                lineno = _parse_call_site_lineno(evidence)
493                if lineno is not None:
494                    n = {**n, "call_site_lineno": lineno}
495                result.append(n)
496
497        for caller_id, evidence, _stub_id in stub_callers:
498            if caller_id in seen:
499                continue
500            if not self._is_compatible_stub_caller(caller_id, evidence, node_id):
501                continue
502            seen.add(caller_id)
503            n = self.node(caller_id)
504            if n:
505                lineno = _parse_call_site_lineno(evidence)
506                if lineno is not None:
507                    n = {**n, "call_site_lineno": lineno}
508                result.append(n)
509
510        return result

Return all nodes that have a rel edge pointing at node_id.

Two-phase lookup:

  1. Direct: edges WHERE dst = node_id AND rel = rel
  2. Indirect: find sym: stubs with RESOLVES_TO edges to node_id and collect their incoming rel edges.
Parameters
  • node_id: Target node identifier.
  • rel: Relation type to invert (default "CALLS").
Returns

List of caller node dicts, deduplicated.

def edges_from( self, node_id: str, *, rel: str = 'CALLS', limit: int | None = None) -> list[dict[str, typing.Any]]: 
573    def edges_from(
574        self, node_id: str, *, rel: str = "CALLS", limit: int | None = None
575    ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
576        """Return all edges originating from *node_id* with the given relation type.
577
578        :param node_id: Source node identifier.
579        :param rel: Relation type to match (default ``"CALLS"``).
580        :param limit: Maximum number of edges to return (``None`` for unlimited).
581        :return: List of edge dicts with keys ``src``, ``rel``, ``dst``, ``evidence``.
582        """
583        query = "SELECT src, rel, dst, evidence FROM edges WHERE src = ? AND rel = ?"
584        params: list[object] = [node_id, rel]
585        if limit is not None:
586            query += " LIMIT ?"
587            params.append(limit)
588        rows = self.con.execute(query, params).fetchall()
589        return [{"src": r[0], "rel": r[1], "dst": r[2], "evidence": r[3]} for r in rows]

Return all edges originating from node_id with the given relation type.

Parameters
  • node_id: Source node identifier.
  • rel: Relation type to match (default "CALLS").
  • limit: Maximum number of edges to return (None for unlimited).
Returns

List of edge dicts with keys src, rel, dst, evidence.

def stats(self) -> dict[str, typing.Any]: 
595    def stats(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
596        """Return node and edge counts by kind/relation, plus domain-specific metrics.
597
598        :return: dict with ``total_nodes``, ``meaningful_nodes``, ``total_edges``,
599                 ``node_counts``, ``edge_counts``, ``docstring_coverage``,
600                 ``snapshot_count``.
601        """
602        node_rows = self.con.execute("SELECT kind, COUNT(*) FROM nodes GROUP BY kind").fetchall()
603        edge_rows = self.con.execute("SELECT rel, COUNT(*) FROM edges GROUP BY rel").fetchall()
604        total_nodes = self.con.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM nodes").fetchone()[0]
605        total_edges = self.con.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM edges").fetchone()[0]
606
607        node_counts: dict[str, int] = {r[0]: r[1] for r in node_rows}
608        symbol_count = node_counts.get("symbol", 0)
609
610        fn_count = node_counts.get("function", 0)
611        method_count = node_counts.get("method", 0)
612        fn_method_total = fn_count + method_count
613        with_doc = self.con.execute(
614            "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM nodes"
615            " WHERE kind IN ('function','method')"
616            " AND docstring IS NOT NULL AND docstring != ''"
617        ).fetchone()[0]
618
619        snapshot_count = 0
620        manifest_path = self.db_path.parent / "snapshots" / "manifest.json"
621        if manifest_path.exists():
622            try:
623                manifest = json.loads(manifest_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
624                snapshot_count = len(manifest.get("snapshots", []))
625            except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError):
626                pass
627
628        return {
629            "db_path": str(self.db_path),
630            "total_nodes": total_nodes,
631            "meaningful_nodes": total_nodes - symbol_count,
632            "total_edges": total_edges,
633            "node_counts": node_counts,
634            "edge_counts": {r[0]: r[1] for r in edge_rows},
635            "module_count": node_counts.get("module", 0),
636            "class_count": node_counts.get("class", 0),
637            "function_count": fn_count,
638            "method_count": method_count,
639            "docstring_coverage": round(with_doc / fn_method_total, 3) if fn_method_total else 0.0,
640            "snapshot_count": snapshot_count,
641        }

class SentenceTransformerEmbedder(pycode_kg.Embedder): 
208class SentenceTransformerEmbedder(Embedder):
209    """Concrete embedder backed by ``sentence-transformers``.
210
211    Delegates model loading to :func:`load_sentence_transformer` so the
212    ``local_files_only`` guard is always in effect.
213
214    :param model_name: HuggingFace model ID or KNOWN_MODELS alias.
215    """
216
217    def __init__(self, model_name: str = DEFAULT_MODEL) -> None:
218        try:
219            hf_logging = importlib.import_module("transformers.logging")
220
221            hf_logging.set_verbosity_error()
222            hf_logging.disable_progress_bar()
223        except (ImportError, ValueError):
224            pass
225
226        _prev = os.environ.get("TQDM_DISABLE")
227        os.environ["TQDM_DISABLE"] = "1"
228        try:
229            self.model = load_sentence_transformer(model_name)
230        finally:
231            if _prev is None:
232                os.environ.pop("TQDM_DISABLE", None)
233            else:
234                os.environ["TQDM_DISABLE"] = _prev
235
236        self.model_name: str = KNOWN_MODELS.get(model_name, model_name)
237        # ST ≥5.4 renamed get_embedding_dimension; ≤5.3 had get_sentence_embedding_dimension.
238        _dim_fn = getattr(self.model, "get_embedding_dimension", None) or getattr(
239            self.model, "get_sentence_embedding_dimension", None
240        )
241        self.dim: int = (_dim_fn() if _dim_fn is not None else None) or 384
242
243    def embed_texts(
244        self, texts: list[str], encode_batch_size: int = DEFAULT_ENCODE_BATCH
245    ) -> list[list[float]]:
246        """Embed a list of strings into float32 vectors.
247
248        :param texts: Input strings.
249        :param encode_batch_size: Per-call ``model.encode`` batch (default
250            :data:`DEFAULT_ENCODE_BATCH`).  Memory scales with ``batch x seq^2``;
251            tune down further if OOM on MPS, up only for large-VRAM CUDA.
252        """
253        np = importlib.import_module("numpy")
254
255        vecs = self.model.encode(
256            texts,
257            batch_size=encode_batch_size,
258            normalize_embeddings=True,
259            show_progress_bar=False,
260        )
261        return [np.asarray(v, dtype="float32").tolist() for v in vecs]
262
263    def embed_query(self, query: str) -> list[float]:
264        """Embed a single query string into a float32 vector."""
265        np = importlib.import_module("numpy")
266
267        vec = self.model.encode([query], normalize_embeddings=True)[0]
268        return list(np.asarray(vec, dtype="float32").tolist())
269
270    def __repr__(self) -> str:
271        return f"SentenceTransformerEmbedder(model={self.model_name!r}, dim={self.dim})"

class SemanticIndex: 
131class SemanticIndex:
132    """LanceDB-backed semantic vector index for a knowledge graph.
133
134    Reads nodes from a :class:`~kg_utils.store.GraphStore`, embeds them, and
135    stores the vectors in LanceDB.  The index is derived and disposable — it
136    can be rebuilt from SQLite at any time without data loss.
137
138    :param lancedb_dir: Directory for the LanceDB database (used only when the
139        default LanceDB backend is constructed; ignored if *backend* is given).
140    :param embedder: Embedding backend. Defaults to :class:`SentenceTransformerEmbedder`.
141    :param table: LanceDB table name.
142    :param index_kinds: Node kinds to embed.
143    :param backend: Vector store backend. Defaults to a :class:`LanceDBBackend`
144        over *lancedb_dir* — pass a :class:`SqliteVecBackend` to store vectors in
145        ``sqlite-vec`` instead.
146    """
147
148    def __init__(
149        self,
150        lancedb_dir: str | Path,
151        *,
152        embedder: Embedder | None = None,
153        table: str = _DEFAULT_TABLE,
154        index_kinds: Sequence[str] = _DEFAULT_KINDS,
155        backend: VectorBackend | None = None,
156    ) -> None:
157        self.lancedb_dir = Path(lancedb_dir)
158        self.embedder: Embedder = embedder or SentenceTransformerEmbedder()
159        self.table_name = table
160        self.index_kinds = tuple(index_kinds)
161        self._backend: VectorBackend | None = backend
162
163    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
164    # Build
165    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
166
167    def build(
168        self,
169        store: GraphStore,
170        *,
171        wipe: bool = False,
172        batch_size: int = 256,
173        quiet: bool = True,
174    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
175        """Build (or rebuild) the vector index from *store*.
176
177        :param store: Authoritative :class:`~kg_utils.store.GraphStore`.
178        :param wipe: If ``True``, delete all existing vectors first.
179        :param batch_size: Number of nodes to embed per batch.
180        :param quiet: Suppress progress output during ingestion.
181        :return: Stats dict with ``indexed_rows``, ``dim``, ``table``, ``lancedb_dir``, ``kinds``.
182        """
183        if quiet:
184            suppress_ingestion_logging()
185
186        nodes = self._read_nodes(store)
187        backend = self._get_backend()
188        backend.open(wipe=wipe)
189
190        indexed = 0
191        for i in range(0, len(nodes), batch_size):
192            chunk = nodes[i : i + batch_size]
193            texts = [_build_index_text(n) for n in chunk]
194            vecs = self.embedder.embed_texts(texts)
195
196            rows = [
197                {
198                    "id": n["id"],
199                    "kind": n["kind"],
200                    "name": n["name"],
201                    "qualname": n["qualname"] or "",
202                    "module_path": n["module_path"] or "",
203                    "text": text,
204                    "vector": vec,
205                }
206                for n, text, vec in zip(chunk, texts, vecs)
207            ]
208            indexed += backend.upsert(rows, batch_size=len(rows))
209
210        # No-op unless the backend is a LanceDBBackend with ANN enabled.
211        if isinstance(backend, LanceDBBackend):
212            backend.maybe_create_ann_index(quiet=quiet)
213
214        return {
215            "indexed_rows": indexed,
216            "dim": self.embedder.dim,
217            "table": self.table_name,
218            "lancedb_dir": str(self.lancedb_dir),
219            "kinds": list(self.index_kinds),
220        }
221
222    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
223    # Search
224    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
225
226    def search(self, query: str, k: int = 8, *, where: str | None = None) -> list[SeedHit]:
227        """Semantic vector search.
228
229        :param query: Natural-language query string.
230        :param k: Number of results to return.
231        :param where: Optional SQL predicate over the metadata columns, applied
232            as a true prefilter (the ``k`` nearest are drawn from the matching
233            subset). Unifies this signature with doc_kg's ``SemanticIndex``.
234        :return: List of :class:`SeedHit` ordered by ascending distance.
235        """
236        backend = self._get_backend()
237        qvec = self.embedder.embed_query(query)
238        raw = backend.search(qvec, k, where=where)
239
240        hits: list[SeedHit] = []
241        for rank, row in enumerate(raw):
242            dist = _extract_distance(row, rank)
243            hits.append(
244                SeedHit(
245                    id=row["id"],
246                    kind=row.get("kind", ""),
247                    name=row.get("name", ""),
248                    qualname=row.get("qualname", ""),
249                    module_path=row.get("module_path", ""),
250                    distance=dist,
251                    rank=rank,
252                )
253            )
254        return hits
255
256    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
257    # Internal helpers
258    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
259
260    def _read_nodes(self, store: GraphStore) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
261        return store.query_nodes(kinds=list(self.index_kinds))
262
263    def _get_backend(self) -> VectorBackend:
264        """Return the vector backend, constructing the default LanceDB one lazily.
265
266        Deferred so the embedder's ``dim`` (which may load the model) is only
267        touched when the index is actually built or searched.
268        """
269        if self._backend is None:
270            self._backend = LanceDBBackend(
271                self.lancedb_dir,
272                table=self.table_name,
273                dim=self.embedder.dim,
274                meta_columns=_META_COLUMNS,
275            )
276        return self._backend
277
278    def __repr__(self) -> str:
279        return (
280            f"SemanticIndex(lancedb_dir={self.lancedb_dir!r}, "
281            f"table={self.table_name!r}, embedder={self.embedder!r})"
282        )

226    def search(self, query: str, k: int = 8, *, where: str | None = None) -> list[SeedHit]:

228
229        :param query: Natural-language query string.
230        :param k: Number of results to return.
231        :param where: Optional SQL predicate over the metadata columns, applied
232            as a true prefilter (the ``k`` nearest are drawn from the matching
233            subset). Unifies this signature with doc_kg's ``SemanticIndex``.
234        :return: List of :class:`SeedHit` ordered by ascending distance.
235        """
236        backend = self._get_backend()
237        qvec = self.embedder.embed_query(query)
238        raw = backend.search(qvec, k, where=where)
239
240        hits: list[SeedHit] = []
241        for rank, row in enumerate(raw):
242            dist = _extract_distance(row, rank)
243            hits.append(
244                SeedHit(
245                    id=row["id"],
246                    kind=row.get("kind", ""),
247                    name=row.get("name", ""),
248                    qualname=row.get("qualname", ""),
249                    module_path=row.get("module_path", ""),
250                    distance=dist,
251                    rank=rank,
252                )
253            )
254        return hits

Semantic vector search.

Parameters
  • query: Natural-language query string.
  • k: Number of results to return.
  • where: Optional SQL predicate over the metadata columns, applied as a true prefilter (the k nearest are drawn from the matching subset). Unifies this signature with doc_kg's SemanticIndex.
Returns

List of SeedHit ordered by ascending distance.

class KGExtractor(abc.ABC): 
14class KGExtractor(ABC):
15    """Abstract extraction protocol for any knowledge graph domain.
16
17    Subclass and implement :meth:`node_kinds`, :meth:`edge_kinds`, and
18    :meth:`extract`.  The concrete :class:`~kg_utils.pipeline.KGModule`
19    infrastructure (:class:`~kg_utils.store.GraphStore`,
20    :class:`~kg_utils.semantic.SemanticIndex`, snapshot management) is
21    provided by the framework — you only implement domain-specific parsing.
22
23    :param repo_path: Absolute path to the repository or corpus root.
24    :param config: Optional domain-specific configuration dict.
25    """
26
27    def __init__(self, repo_path: Path, config: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> None:
28        self.repo_path = Path(repo_path).resolve()
29        self.config = config or {}
30
31    @abstractmethod
32    def node_kinds(self) -> list[str]:
33        """Return canonical node kind names emitted by this extractor.
34
35        :return: List of node kind strings (e.g. ``['module', 'class', 'function']``).
36        """
37
38    @abstractmethod
39    def edge_kinds(self) -> list[str]:
40        """Return canonical edge relation types emitted by this extractor.
41
42        :return: List of edge relation strings (e.g. ``['CONTAINS', 'CALLS']``).
43        """
44
45    @abstractmethod
46    def extract(self) -> Iterator[NodeSpec | EdgeSpec]:
47        """Traverse the source and yield NodeSpec / EdgeSpec objects.
48
49        Implementations must be deterministic: the same source should produce
50        the same stream on every call.
51
52        :return: Iterator of :class:`NodeSpec` and :class:`EdgeSpec` objects.
53        """
54
55    def meaningful_node_kinds(self) -> list[str]:
56        """Return node kinds included in the vector index and coverage metrics.
57
58        Default: all of :meth:`node_kinds`.  Override to exclude structural
59        stubs (e.g., unresolved import placeholders) from semantic indexing.
60
61        :return: Subset of node_kinds() to index semantically.
62        """
63        return self.node_kinds()
64
65    def coverage_metric(self, nodes: list[NodeSpec]) -> float:
66        """Compute a domain coverage quality metric.
67
68        Default: fraction of meaningful nodes with a non-empty docstring.
69
70        :param nodes: All extracted NodeSpec objects.
71        :return: Coverage score in [0.0, 1.0].
72        """
73        meaningful = [n for n in nodes if n.kind in self.meaningful_node_kinds()]
74        if not meaningful:
75            return 0.0
76        covered = sum(1 for n in meaningful if n.docstring.strip())
77        return covered / len(meaningful)

class PyCodeKGExtractor(pycode_kg.KGExtractor): 
 28class PyCodeKGExtractor(KGExtractor):
 29    """KGExtractor backed by CodeGraph (Python AST analysis).
 30
 31    Wraps :class:`~pycode_kg.graph.CodeGraph` and converts its :class:`Node`
 32    and :class:`Edge` v0 primitives to :class:`NodeSpec` / :class:`EdgeSpec`
 33    for the generic :class:`~pycode_kg.module.base.KGModule` build pipeline.
 34
 35    This is the extractor used by :class:`~pycode_kg.kg.PyCodeKG` and is the
 36    reference implementation for source-code KG extractors.
 37
 38    :param repo_path: Path to the Python repository root.
 39    :param include: Set of top-level directory names to include (all if empty).
 40    :param exclude: Set of directory names to exclude at every depth.
 41    :param config: Optional config dict (forwarded to super).
 42    """
 43
 44    def __init__(
 45        self,
 46        repo_path: Path,
 47        *,
 48        include: set[str] | None = None,
 49        exclude: set[str] | None = None,
 50        config: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
 51    ) -> None:
 52        """Initialise the extractor for a Python repository.
 53
 54        :param repo_path: Path to the Python repository root.
 55        :param include: Top-level directory names to include (empty = all).
 56        :param exclude: Directory names to exclude at every walk depth.
 57        :param config: Optional domain-specific configuration dict.
 58        """
 59        super().__init__(repo_path, config)
 60        self._include: set[str] = include or set()
 61        self._exclude: set[str] = exclude or set()
 62
 63    def node_kinds(self) -> list[str]:
 64        """Return the Python AST node kinds.
 65
 66        :return: ``['module', 'class', 'function', 'method', 'symbol']``
 67        """
 68        return ["module", "class", "function", "method", "symbol"]
 69
 70    def edge_kinds(self) -> list[str]:
 71        """Return the Python AST edge relation types.
 72
 73        :return: List of all relation strings emitted by the Python extractor.
 74        """
 75        return [
 76            "CONTAINS",
 77            "CALLS",
 78            "IMPORTS",
 79            "INHERITS",
 80            "READS",
 81            "WRITES",
 82            "ATTR_ACCESS",
 83            "DEPENDS_ON",
 84            "RESOLVES_TO",
 85        ]
 86
 87    def meaningful_node_kinds(self) -> list[str]:
 88        """Return the node kinds indexed in the vector store and counted in coverage.
 89
 90        Excludes ``'symbol'`` (unresolved import stubs).
 91
 92        :return: ``['module', 'class', 'function', 'method']``
 93        """
 94        return ["module", "class", "function", "method"]
 95
 96    def extract(self) -> Iterator[NodeSpec | EdgeSpec]:
 97        """Run Python AST extraction and yield NodeSpec / EdgeSpec objects.
 98
 99        Delegates to :class:`~pycode_kg.graph.CodeGraph` for the AST walk, then
100        converts the v0-locked :class:`~pycode_kg.pycodekg.Node` and
101        :class:`~pycode_kg.pycodekg.Edge` primitives to the generic spec types.
102
103        :return: Iterator of :class:`NodeSpec` and :class:`EdgeSpec` objects.
104        """
105        from pycode_kg.graph import CodeGraph  # noqa: PLC0415
106
107        graph = CodeGraph(self.repo_path, include=self._include, exclude=self._exclude)
108        nodes, edges = graph.result()
109
110        for n in nodes:
111            yield NodeSpec(
112                node_id=n.id,
113                kind=n.kind,
114                name=n.name,
115                qualname=n.qualname or "",
116                source_path=n.module_path or "",
117                lineno=n.lineno,
118                end_lineno=n.end_lineno,
119                docstring=n.docstring or "",
120            )
121
122        for e in edges:
123            yield EdgeSpec(
124                source_id=e.src,
125                target_id=e.dst,
126                relation=e.rel,
127                metadata={"evidence": e.evidence} if e.evidence else {},
128            )

class PyCodeKG(pycode_kg.KGModule): 
 65class PyCodeKG(KGModule):
 66    """
 67    Top-level orchestrator for the Code Knowledge Graph.
 68
 69    Subclasses :class:`~pycode_kg.module.base.KGModule` and provides the
 70    Python-AST-specific extraction layer via :class:`PyCodeKGExtractor`.
 71    All generic infrastructure — SQLite persistence, sqlite-vec indexing,
 72    hybrid query, snippet packing, snapshots — is inherited from
 73    :class:`~pycode_kg.module.base.KGModule`.
 74
 75    Typical usage::
 76
 77        kg = PyCodeKG(repo_root="/path/to/repo")
 78        stats = kg.build(wipe=True)
 79        print(stats)
 80
 81        result = kg.query("database connection setup", k=8, hop=1)
 82        result.print_summary()
 83
 84        pack = kg.pack("configuration loading", k=8, hop=1)
 85        pack.save("context.md")
 86
 87    :param repo_root: Repository root directory.
 88    :param db_path: SQLite database path (defaults to
 89        ``<repo_root>/.pycodekg/graph.sqlite``).
 90    :param vectors_path: sqlite-vec vector store path (defaults to
 91        ``<repo_root>/.pycodekg/vectors.sqlite``).
 92    :param model: Sentence-transformer model name.
 93    """
 94
 95    _default_dir = ".pycodekg"
 96
 97    def __init__(
 98        self,
 99        repo_root: str | Path,
100        db_path: str | Path | None = None,
101        vectors_path: str | Path | None = None,
102        *,
103        model: str = DEFAULT_MODEL,
104    ) -> None:
105        """Initialise ``PyCodeKG`` and resolve all paths.
106
107        :param repo_root: Repository root directory; resolved to an absolute path.
108        :param db_path: Path to the SQLite database file.
109        :param vectors_path: Path to the sqlite-vec vector store file.
110        :param model: Sentence-transformer model name used for embedding.
111        """
112        super().__init__(
113            repo_root,
114            db_path=db_path,
115            model=model,
116            vector_backend="sqlite-vec",
117        )
118        if vectors_path is not None:
119            self.vectors_path = Path(vectors_path)
120        # Backwards-compatible cached CodeGraph (direct access still works)
121        self._graph: CodeGraph | None = None
122
123    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
124    # KGModule abstract interface
125    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
126
127    def make_extractor(self) -> KGExtractor:
128        """Return a PyCodeKGExtractor for this repository.
129
130        :return: :class:`PyCodeKGExtractor` targeting :attr:`repo_root`.
131        """
132        return PyCodeKGExtractor(self.repo_root)
133
134    def kind(self) -> str:
135        """Return the KG kind string.
136
137        :return: ``"code"``
138        """
139        return "code"
140
141    def analyze(self, *, include_edge_provenance: bool = False) -> str:
142        """Run full nine-phase architectural analysis and return Markdown.
143
144        Delegates to :class:`~pycode_kg.pycodekg_thorough_analysis.PyCodeKGAnalyzer`.
145        This is the same analysis produced by ``pycodekg analyze``.
146
147        :param include_edge_provenance: Annotate edges with confidence metadata.
148        :return: Markdown-formatted architectural analysis report.
149        """
150        try:
151            from io import StringIO  # noqa: PLC0415
152
153            from rich.console import Console  # noqa: PLC0415
154
155            from pycode_kg.pycodekg_thorough_analysis import (  # noqa: PLC0415
156                PyCodeKGAnalyzer,
157            )
158
159            silent = Console(file=StringIO(), highlight=False)
160            analyzer = PyCodeKGAnalyzer(self, console=silent)
161            analyzer.run_analysis()
162            return analyzer.to_markdown()
163        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
164            return f"# PyCodeKG Analysis\n\nAnalysis failed: {exc}\n"

168    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
169
170    def _kind_priority(self, kind: str) -> int:
171        """Return Python-specific node kind sort priority.
172
173        :param kind: Node kind string.
174        :return: Integer priority (lower = ranked first).
175        """
176        return _PYCODEKG_KIND_PRIORITY.get(kind, 99)
177
178    def _post_build_hook(self, store: GraphStore) -> None:
179        """Resolve Python symbol stubs after writing nodes/edges.
180
181        Called by :meth:`~pycode_kg.module.base.KGModule.build_graph` after
182        ``store.write()``.  Links ``sym:`` import stubs to their definitions
183        via ``RESOLVES_TO`` edges.
184
185        :param store: The :class:`~pycode_kg.store.GraphStore` just written to.
186        """
187        store.resolve_symbols()

199        :meth:`make_extractor` instead.
200        """

209    def __repr__(self) -> str:
210        """Return an unambiguous string representation.
211
212        :return: ``PyCodeKG(repo_root=..., db_path=..., vectors_path=..., model=...)``.
213        """
214        return (
215            f"PyCodeKG(repo_root={self.repo_root!r}, "
216            f"db_path={self.db_path!r}, "
217            f"vectors_path={self.vectors_path!r}, "
218            f"model={self.model_name!r})"
219        )

Top-level orchestrator for the Code Knowledge Graph.

Subclasses ~pycode_kg.module.base.KGModule and provides the Python-AST-specific extraction layer via PyCodeKGExtractor. All generic infrastructure — SQLite persistence, sqlite-vec indexing, hybrid query, snippet packing, snapshots — is inherited from ~pycode_kg.module.base.KGModule.

Typical usage::

kg = PyCodeKG(repo_root="/path/to/repo")
stats = kg.build(wipe=True)
print(stats)

result = kg.query("database connection setup", k=8, hop=1)
result.print_summary()

pack = kg.pack("configuration loading", k=8, hop=1)
pack.save("context.md")
Parameters

  • db_path: SQLite database path (defaults to <repo_root>/.pycodekg/graph.sqlite).
  • vectors_path: sqlite-vec vector store path (defaults to <repo_root>/.pycodekg/vectors.sqlite).
  • model: Sentence-transformer model name.

106    """Result container returned by KGModule.query().
107
108    :param query: The original query string.
109    :param nodes: List of matched node dicts.
110    :param edges: List of matched edge dicts.
111    :param seeds: Number of seed nodes from vector search.
112    :param expanded_nodes: Number of nodes after graph expansion.
113    :param returned_nodes: Number of nodes actually returned.
114    :param hop: Number of hops used in graph expansion.
115    :param rels: Relation types used in expansion.
116    """
117
118    query: str = ""
119    nodes: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)
120    edges: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)
121    seeds: int = 0
122    expanded_nodes: int = 0
123    returned_nodes: int = 0
124    hop: int = 0
125    rels: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
126
127    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
128        """Serialise the query result to a plain dictionary."""
129        return {
130            "query": self.query,
131            "seeds": self.seeds,
132            "expanded_nodes": self.expanded_nodes,
133            "returned_nodes": self.returned_nodes,
134            "hop": self.hop,
135            "rels": self.rels,
136            "nodes": self.nodes,
137            "edges": self.edges,
138        }
139
140    def to_json(self, *, indent: int = 2) -> str:
141        """Serialise to JSON string."""
142        return json.dumps(self.to_dict(), indent=indent, ensure_ascii=False)
143
144    def print_summary(self) -> None:
145        """Print a human-readable summary to stdout."""
146        sep = "=" * 80
147        print(sep)
148        print(f"QUERY: {self.query}")
149        print(
150            f"Seeds: {self.seeds} | Expanded: {self.expanded_nodes} "
151            f"| Returned: {self.returned_nodes} | hop={self.hop}"
152        )
153        print(f"Rels: {', '.join(self.rels)}")
154        print(sep)
155        for n in self.nodes:
156            print(
157                f"{n['kind']:8s} {(n.get('module_path') or ''):40s} "
158                f"{n.get('qualname') or n['name']}  [{n['id']}]"
159            )
160            if n.get("docstring"):
161                ds0 = n["docstring"].strip().splitlines()[0]
162                print(f"    {ds0[:120]}")
163            print()
164        print("-" * 80)
165        print(f"EDGES (within returned set): {len(self.edges)}")
166        print("-" * 80)
167        for e in sorted(self.edges, key=lambda x: (x["rel"], x["src"], x["dst"])):
168            print(f"  {e['src']} -[{e['rel']}]-> {e['dst']}")
169        print(sep)

@dataclass
class SnippetPack: 
172@dataclass
173class SnippetPack:
174    """Result container returned by KGModule.pack().
175
176    :param query: The original query string.
177    :param seeds: Number of seed nodes from vector search.
178    :param expanded_nodes: Number of nodes after graph expansion.
179    :param returned_nodes: Number of nodes actually returned.
180    :param hop: Number of hops used in expansion.
181    :param rels: Relation types used in expansion.
182    :param model: Embedding model identifier.
183    :param nodes: Node dicts included in the pack (each may have a ``snippet`` key).
184    :param edges: Edge dicts included in the pack.
185    :param snippets: Source-code snippets (for code KGs).
186    :param warnings: Non-fatal issues encountered during packing.
187    """
188
189    query: str
190    seeds: int = 0
191    expanded_nodes: int = 0
192    returned_nodes: int = 0
193    hop: int = 0
194    rels: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
195    model: str = ""
196    nodes: list[Any] = field(default_factory=list)
197    edges: list[Any] = field(default_factory=list)
198    snippets: list[Any] = field(default_factory=list)
199    warnings: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
200
201    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
202        """Serialise the snippet pack to a plain dictionary."""
203        return {
204            "query": self.query,
205            "seeds": self.seeds,
206            "expanded_nodes": self.expanded_nodes,
207            "returned_nodes": self.returned_nodes,
208            "hop": self.hop,
209            "rels": self.rels,
210            "model": self.model,
211            "nodes": self.nodes,
212            "edges": self.edges,
213            "warnings": self.warnings,
214        }
215
216    def to_json(self, *, indent: int = 2) -> str:
217        """Serialise to JSON string."""
218        return json.dumps(self.to_dict(), indent=indent, ensure_ascii=False)
219
220    def to_markdown(self) -> str:
221        """Render the snippet pack as a Markdown context document."""
222        out: list[str] = []
223        out.append("# KGModule Snippet Pack\n")
224        out.append(f"**Query:** `{self.query}`  ")
225        out.append(f"**Seeds:** {self.seeds}  ")
226        out.append(f"**Expanded nodes:** {self.expanded_nodes} (returned: {self.returned_nodes})  ")
227        out.append(f"**hop:** {self.hop}  ")
228        out.append(f"**rels:** {', '.join(self.rels)}  ")
229        out.append(f"**model:** {self.model}  ")
230        out.append("\n---\n")
231
232        if self.warnings:
233            out.append("## Warnings\n")
234            for w in self.warnings:
235                out.append(f"- {w}")
236            out.append("")
237
238        out.append("## Nodes\n")
239        for n in self.nodes:
240            out.append(f"### {n['kind']} — `{n.get('qualname') or n['name']}`")
241            out.append(f"- id: `{n['id']}`")
242            if n.get("module_path"):
243                out.append(f"- module: `{n['module_path']}`")
244            if n.get("lineno") is not None:
245                out.append(f"- line: {n['lineno']}")
246            if n.get("docstring"):
247                ds0 = n["docstring"].strip().splitlines()[0]
248                out.append(f"- doc: {ds0[:140]}")
249            if n.get("relevance"):
250                rel = n["relevance"]
251                _score = rel.get("score", 0.0)
252                _tier = "HIGH" if _score >= 0.60 else ("MEDIUM" if _score >= 0.45 else "LOW")
253                out.append(
254                    "- relevance: "
255                    f"{_score:.3f} [{_tier}] "
256                    f"(semantic={rel.get('semantic', 0.0):.3f}, "
257                    f"lexical={rel.get('lexical', 0.0):.3f}, "
258                    f"docstring_signal={rel.get('docstring_signal', 0.0):.3f}, "
259                    f"hop={rel.get('hop', 0)})"
260                )
261            sn = n.get("snippet")
262            if sn:
263                end_lineno = n.get("end_lineno")
264                if end_lineno is not None and sn["end"] < end_lineno:
265                    out.append(
266                        f"*(truncated: showing lines {sn['start']}–{sn['end']} "
267                        f"of {n.get('lineno', sn['start'])}–{end_lineno})*"
268                    )
269                out.append("")
270                out.append(f"```\n{sn['text']}\n```")
271            out.append("")
272
273        out.append("\n---\n")
274        out.append("## Edges\n")
275        for e in self.edges:
276            out.append(f"- `{e['src']}` -[{e['rel']}]-> `{e['dst']}`")
277        out.append("")
278        return "\n".join(out)
279
280    def save(self, path: str | Path, *, fmt: str = "md") -> None:
281        """Write the pack to a file.
282
283        :param path: Output file path.
284        :param fmt: ``"md"`` for Markdown or ``"json"`` for JSON.
285        """
286        text = self.to_markdown() if fmt == "md" else self.to_json()
287        Path(path).write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")

228        out.append(f"**rels:** {', '.join(self.rels)}  ")
229        out.append(f"**model:** {self.model}  ")
230        out.append("\n---\n")
231
232        if self.warnings:
233            out.append("## Warnings\n")
234            for w in self.warnings:
235                out.append(f"- {w}")
236            out.append("")
237
238        out.append("## Nodes\n")
239        for n in self.nodes:
240            out.append(f"### {n['kind']} — `{n.get('qualname') or n['name']}`")
241            out.append(f"- id: `{n['id']}`")
242            if n.get("module_path"):
243                out.append(f"- module: `{n['module_path']}`")
244            if n.get("lineno") is not None:
245                out.append(f"- line: {n['lineno']}")
246            if n.get("docstring"):
247                ds0 = n["docstring"].strip().splitlines()[0]
248                out.append(f"- doc: {ds0[:140]}")
249            if n.get("relevance"):
250                rel = n["relevance"]
251                _score = rel.get("score", 0.0)
252                _tier = "HIGH" if _score >= 0.60 else ("MEDIUM" if _score >= 0.45 else "LOW")
253                out.append(
254                    "- relevance: "
255                    f"{_score:.3f} [{_tier}] "
256                    f"(semantic={rel.get('semantic', 0.0):.3f}, "
257                    f"lexical={rel.get('lexical', 0.0):.3f}, "
258                    f"docstring_signal={rel.get('docstring_signal', 0.0):.3f}, "
259                    f"hop={rel.get('hop', 0)})"
260                )
261            sn = n.get("snippet")
262            if sn:
263                end_lineno = n.get("end_lineno")
264                if end_lineno is not None and sn["end"] < end_lineno:
265                    out.append(
266                        f"*(truncated: showing lines {sn['start']}–{sn['end']} "
267                        f"of {n.get('lineno', sn['start'])}–{end_lineno})*"
268                    )
269                out.append("")
270                out.append(f"```\n{sn['text']}\n```")
271            out.append("")
272
273        out.append("\n---\n")
274        out.append("## Edges\n")
275        for e in self.edges:
276            out.append(f"- `{e['src']}` -[{e['rel']}]-> `{e['dst']}`")
277        out.append("")
278        return "\n".join(out)

178    remain plain dicts on disk; the properties are view-only adapters.
179

181    -------------------
182    Python dataclass fields are stored in ``__dict__`` under their field name.
183    The properties below always read and write the raw dict stored in
184    ``self.__dict__`` directly so that the shared base-class infrastructure
185    (which expects plain dicts) continues to work without modification.
186    """

193    @metrics.setter

241        base = _BaseSnapshot.from_dict(data)
