class SnapshotManager(kg_utils.snapshots.manager.SnapshotManager): 
250class SnapshotManager(_BaseSnapshotManager):
251    """pycode-kg snapshot manager.
252
253    Subclasses the shared ``kg_utils.snapshots.SnapshotManager`` and adds:
254
255    * ``package_name="pycode-kg"`` default for version detection.
256    * Legacy ``capture()`` kwargs: ``coverage``, ``critical_issues``,
257      ``complexity_median`` — merged into the metrics dict.
258    * ``_compute_delta_from_metrics`` extended with ``coverage_delta`` and
259      ``critical_issues_delta``.
260    * ``_collect_module_node_counts()`` — SQLite per-module node counts stored
261      in snapshot metrics under ``"module_node_counts"``.
262    * Returns ``pycode_kg.snapshots.Snapshot`` instances (with typed-accessor
263      properties) from all load/capture methods.
264    """
265
266    def __init__(
267        self,
268        snapshots_dir: Path | str,
269        *,
270        db_path: Path | str | None = None,
271        package_name: str = "pycode-kg",
272    ) -> None:
273        """Initialize the manager rooted at ``snapshots_dir``.
274
275        :param snapshots_dir: Directory where snapshot JSON files live; created
276            on first save if it does not exist.
277        :param db_path: PyCodeKG SQLite graph path; required for collecting
278            per-module node counts during ``capture()``. Optional otherwise.
279        :param package_name: Package name used for version detection in saved
280            snapshots. Defaults to ``"pycode-kg"``.
281        """
282        super().__init__(snapshots_dir, package_name=package_name, db_path=db_path)
283
284    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
285    # capture — backwards-compat wrapper
286    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
287
288    def capture(  # ty: ignore[invalid-method-override]
289        self,
290        version: str | None = None,
291        branch: str | None = None,
292        graph_stats_dict: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
293        coverage: float = 0.0,
294        critical_issues: int = 0,
295        complexity_median: float = 0.0,
296        hotspots: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None,
297        issues: list[str] | None = None,
298        tree_hash: str = "",
299    ) -> Snapshot:
300        """Capture a pycode-kg snapshot.
301
302        Accepts the legacy per-field kwargs (``coverage``, ``critical_issues``,
303        ``complexity_median``) in addition to the dict-based
304        ``graph_stats_dict`` from the base class, and builds the full metrics
305        dict expected by the shared infrastructure.
306
307        :param version: Version string (e.g., "0.5.1").
308        :param branch: Git branch name; auto-detected if None.
309        :param graph_stats_dict: Output from ``graph_stats()`` / ``store.stats()``.
310        :param coverage: Docstring coverage fraction (0.0–1.0).
311        :param critical_issues: Number of critical issues detected.
312        :param complexity_median: Median fan-in across functions.
313        :param hotspots: Top hotspot entries.
314        :param issues: Issue description strings.
315        :param tree_hash: Git tree hash; auto-detected if not provided.
316        :return: New :class:`Snapshot` instance (not yet persisted).
317        """
318        module_node_counts = self._collect_module_node_counts()
319
320        base_snap = super().capture(
321            version=version,
322            branch=branch,
323            graph_stats_dict=graph_stats_dict,
324            tree_hash=tree_hash,
325            hotspots=hotspots,
326            issues=issues,
327            docstring_coverage=coverage,
328            critical_issues=critical_issues,
329            complexity_median=complexity_median,
330            module_node_counts=module_node_counts,
331        )
332
333        return _rewrap(base_snap)
334
335    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
336    # diff_snapshots — adds module_node_counts_delta and issues_delta
337    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
338
339    def diff_snapshots(self, key_a: str, key_b: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
340        """Compare two snapshots side-by-side.
341
342        Extends the base diff with ``module_node_counts_delta`` and
343        ``issues_delta`` (introduced / resolved issue strings).
344
345        :param key_a: First snapshot key (tree hash).
346        :param key_b: Second snapshot key (tree hash).
347        :return: Dict with metrics from both, computed deltas.
348        """
349        snap_a = _BaseSnapshotManager.load_snapshot(self, key_a)
350        snap_b = _BaseSnapshotManager.load_snapshot(self, key_b)
351
352        if not snap_a or not snap_b:
353            return {"error": "One or both snapshots not found"}
354
355        m_a = snap_a.metrics
356        m_b = snap_b.metrics
357
358        all_node_kinds = set(m_a.get("node_counts", {})) | set(m_b.get("node_counts", {}))
359        all_edge_rels = set(m_a.get("edge_counts", {})) | set(m_b.get("edge_counts", {}))
360
361        node_counts_delta = {
362            k: m_b.get("node_counts", {}).get(k, 0) - m_a.get("node_counts", {}).get(k, 0)
363            for k in all_node_kinds
364        }
365        edge_counts_delta = {
366            k: m_b.get("edge_counts", {}).get(k, 0) - m_a.get("edge_counts", {}).get(k, 0)
367            for k in all_edge_rels
368        }
369
370        all_modules = set(m_a.get("module_node_counts", {})) | set(
371            m_b.get("module_node_counts", {})
372        )
373        module_node_counts_delta = {
374            mod: m_b.get("module_node_counts", {}).get(mod, 0)
375            - m_a.get("module_node_counts", {}).get(mod, 0)
376            for mod in all_modules
377            if m_b.get("module_node_counts", {}).get(mod, 0)
378            != m_a.get("module_node_counts", {}).get(mod, 0)
379        }
380
381        issues_a = set(snap_a.issues)
382        issues_b = set(snap_b.issues)
383
384        return {
385            "a": {
386                "key": snap_a.key,
387                "metrics": m_a,
388                "issues": snap_a.issues,
389                "timestamp": snap_a.timestamp,
390            },
391            "b": {
392                "key": snap_b.key,
393                "metrics": m_b,
394                "issues": snap_b.issues,
395                "timestamp": snap_b.timestamp,
396            },
397            "delta": self._compute_delta_from_metrics(m_b, m_a),
398            "node_counts_delta": node_counts_delta,
399            "edge_counts_delta": edge_counts_delta,
400            "module_node_counts_delta": module_node_counts_delta,
401            "issues_delta": {
402                "introduced": list(issues_b - issues_a),
403                "resolved": list(issues_a - issues_b),
404            },
405        }
406
407    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
408    # Delta computation — adds coverage_delta and critical_issues_delta
409    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
410
411    def _compute_delta(self, snap_new: _BaseSnapshot, snap_old: _BaseSnapshot) -> dict[str, Any]:
412        """Compute delta, extracting raw metric dicts to avoid the typed-property layer."""
413        new_m = snap_new.__dict__.get("metrics", snap_new.metrics)
414        old_m = snap_old.__dict__.get("metrics", snap_old.metrics)
415        if isinstance(new_m, SnapshotMetrics):
416            new_m = metrics_to_dict(new_m)
417        if isinstance(old_m, SnapshotMetrics):
418            old_m = metrics_to_dict(old_m)
419        return self._compute_delta_from_metrics(new_m, old_m)
420
421    def _compute_delta_from_metrics(
422        self, new_m: dict[str, Any], old_m: dict[str, Any]
423    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
424        """Compute delta dict including pycode-kg specific fields."""
425        return {
426            "nodes": new_m.get("total_nodes", 0) - old_m.get("total_nodes", 0),
427            "edges": new_m.get("total_edges", 0) - old_m.get("total_edges", 0),
428            "coverage_delta": (
429                new_m.get("docstring_coverage", 0.0) - old_m.get("docstring_coverage", 0.0)
430            ),
431            "critical_issues_delta": (
432                new_m.get("critical_issues", 0) - old_m.get("critical_issues", 0)
433            ),
434        }
435
436    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
437    # save_snapshot — normalise typed properties back to raw dicts first
438    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
439
440    def save_snapshot(self, snapshot: _BaseSnapshot, *, force: bool = False) -> Any:
441        """Persist snapshot, normalising any typed-property values to raw dicts.
442
443        The base ``save_snapshot`` inspects ``snapshot.metrics`` (expects a
444        dict) and ``snapshot.vs_previous`` / ``snapshot.vs_baseline`` (expects
445        dicts or None) directly.  If ``snapshot`` is a pycode-kg ``Snapshot``
446        the properties return typed dataclasses instead; we substitute a plain
447        ``_BaseSnapshot`` carrying the raw dicts so the base implementation
448        can serialise without modification.
449        """
450        if isinstance(snapshot, Snapshot):
451            raw = _BaseSnapshot(
452                branch=snapshot.branch,
453                timestamp=snapshot.timestamp,
454                version=snapshot.version,
455                metrics=snapshot.__dict__["metrics"],
456                hotspots=snapshot.hotspots,
457                issues=snapshot.issues,
458                vs_previous=snapshot.__dict__["vs_previous"],
459                vs_baseline=snapshot.__dict__["vs_baseline"],
460                tree_hash=snapshot.tree_hash,
461            )
462            return super().save_snapshot(raw, force=force)
463        return super().save_snapshot(snapshot, force=force)
464
465    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
466    # Load helpers — re-wrap base Snapshot instances as pycode-kg Snapshots
467    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
468
469    def load_snapshot(self, key: str) -> Snapshot | None:  # type: ignore[override]
470        """Load a snapshot by key and re-wrap it as a pycode-kg ``Snapshot`` with typed-accessor properties. Returns ``None`` if no snapshot matches."""
471        snap = super().load_snapshot(key)
472        return _rewrap(snap) if snap is not None else None
473
474    def get_previous(self, key: str) -> Snapshot | None:  # type: ignore[override]
475        """Return the snapshot immediately preceding ``key`` in manifest chronology, re-wrapped as a pycode-kg ``Snapshot``. ``None`` when ``key`` is the earliest."""
476        snap = super().get_previous(key)
477        return _rewrap(snap) if snap is not None else None
478
479    def get_baseline(self) -> Snapshot | None:  # type: ignore[override]
480        """Return the earliest (baseline) snapshot in the manifest, re-wrapped as a pycode-kg ``Snapshot``. ``None`` if no snapshots exist."""
481        snap = super().get_baseline()
482        return _rewrap(snap) if snap is not None else None
483
484    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
485    # SQLite per-module node counts
486    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
487
488    def _collect_module_node_counts(self) -> dict[str, int]:
489        """Query SQLite for per-module node counts.
490
491        :return: Dict mapping ``module_path`` to node count, or ``{}`` if the
492                 database is unavailable or the query fails.
493        """
494        if not self.db_path or not self.db_path.exists():
495            return {}
496        try:
497            with sqlite3.connect(self.db_path) as conn:
498                rows = conn.execute(
499                    "SELECT module_path, COUNT(*) FROM nodes GROUP BY module_path"
500                ).fetchall()
501            return {row[0]: row[1] for row in rows if row[0]}
502        except sqlite3.Error:
503            return {}

295        complexity_median: float = 0.0,

297        issues: list[str] | None = None,
298        tree_hash: str = "",
299    ) -> Snapshot:
300        """Capture a pycode-kg snapshot.
301
302        Accepts the legacy per-field kwargs (``coverage``, ``critical_issues``,
303        ``complexity_median``) in addition to the dict-based
304        ``graph_stats_dict`` from the base class, and builds the full metrics
305        dict expected by the shared infrastructure.
306
307        :param version: Version string (e.g., "0.5.1").
308        :param branch: Git branch name; auto-detected if None.
309        :param graph_stats_dict: Output from ``graph_stats()`` / ``store.stats()``.
310        :param coverage: Docstring coverage fraction (0.0–1.0).
311        :param critical_issues: Number of critical issues detected.
312        :param complexity_median: Median fan-in across functions.
313        :param hotspots: Top hotspot entries.
314        :param issues: Issue description strings.
315        :param tree_hash: Git tree hash; auto-detected if not provided.
316        :return: New :class:`Snapshot` instance (not yet persisted).
317        """
318        module_node_counts = self._collect_module_node_counts()
319
320        base_snap = super().capture(
321            version=version,
322            branch=branch,
323            graph_stats_dict=graph_stats_dict,
324            tree_hash=tree_hash,
325            hotspots=hotspots,
326            issues=issues,
327            docstring_coverage=coverage,
328            critical_issues=critical_issues,
329            complexity_median=complexity_median,
330            module_node_counts=module_node_counts,
331        )
332
333        return _rewrap(base_snap)

def diff_snapshots(self, key_a: str, key_b: str) -> dict[str, typing.Any]: 
339    def diff_snapshots(self, key_a: str, key_b: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
340        """Compare two snapshots side-by-side.
341
342        Extends the base diff with ``module_node_counts_delta`` and
343        ``issues_delta`` (introduced / resolved issue strings).
344
345        :param key_a: First snapshot key (tree hash).
346        :param key_b: Second snapshot key (tree hash).
347        :return: Dict with metrics from both, computed deltas.
348        """
349        snap_a = _BaseSnapshotManager.load_snapshot(self, key_a)
350        snap_b = _BaseSnapshotManager.load_snapshot(self, key_b)
351
352        if not snap_a or not snap_b:
353            return {"error": "One or both snapshots not found"}
354
355        m_a = snap_a.metrics
356        m_b = snap_b.metrics
357
358        all_node_kinds = set(m_a.get("node_counts", {})) | set(m_b.get("node_counts", {}))
359        all_edge_rels = set(m_a.get("edge_counts", {})) | set(m_b.get("edge_counts", {}))
360
361        node_counts_delta = {
362            k: m_b.get("node_counts", {}).get(k, 0) - m_a.get("node_counts", {}).get(k, 0)
363            for k in all_node_kinds
364        }
365        edge_counts_delta = {
366            k: m_b.get("edge_counts", {}).get(k, 0) - m_a.get("edge_counts", {}).get(k, 0)
367            for k in all_edge_rels
368        }
369
370        all_modules = set(m_a.get("module_node_counts", {})) | set(
371            m_b.get("module_node_counts", {})
372        )
373        module_node_counts_delta = {
374            mod: m_b.get("module_node_counts", {}).get(mod, 0)
375            - m_a.get("module_node_counts", {}).get(mod, 0)
376            for mod in all_modules
377            if m_b.get("module_node_counts", {}).get(mod, 0)
378            != m_a.get("module_node_counts", {}).get(mod, 0)
379        }
380
381        issues_a = set(snap_a.issues)
382        issues_b = set(snap_b.issues)
383
384        return {
385            "a": {
386                "key": snap_a.key,
387                "metrics": m_a,
388                "issues": snap_a.issues,
389                "timestamp": snap_a.timestamp,
390            },
391            "b": {
392                "key": snap_b.key,
393                "metrics": m_b,
394                "issues": snap_b.issues,
395                "timestamp": snap_b.timestamp,
396            },
397            "delta": self._compute_delta_from_metrics(m_b, m_a),
398            "node_counts_delta": node_counts_delta,
399            "edge_counts_delta": edge_counts_delta,
400            "module_node_counts_delta": module_node_counts_delta,
401            "issues_delta": {
402                "introduced": list(issues_b - issues_a),
403                "resolved": list(issues_a - issues_b),
404            },
405        }

def save_snapshot( self, snapshot: kg_utils.snapshots.models.Snapshot, *, force: bool = False) -> Any: 
440    def save_snapshot(self, snapshot: _BaseSnapshot, *, force: bool = False) -> Any:
441        """Persist snapshot, normalising any typed-property values to raw dicts.
442
443        The base ``save_snapshot`` inspects ``snapshot.metrics`` (expects a
444        dict) and ``snapshot.vs_previous`` / ``snapshot.vs_baseline`` (expects
445        dicts or None) directly.  If ``snapshot`` is a pycode-kg ``Snapshot``
446        the properties return typed dataclasses instead; we substitute a plain
447        ``_BaseSnapshot`` carrying the raw dicts so the base implementation
448        can serialise without modification.
449        """
450        if isinstance(snapshot, Snapshot):
451            raw = _BaseSnapshot(
452                branch=snapshot.branch,
453                timestamp=snapshot.timestamp,
454                version=snapshot.version,
455                metrics=snapshot.__dict__["metrics"],
456                hotspots=snapshot.hotspots,
457                issues=snapshot.issues,
458                vs_previous=snapshot.__dict__["vs_previous"],
459                vs_baseline=snapshot.__dict__["vs_baseline"],
460                tree_hash=snapshot.tree_hash,
461            )
462            return super().save_snapshot(raw, force=force)
463        return super().save_snapshot(snapshot, force=force)

Persist snapshot, normalising any typed-property values to raw dicts.

The base save_snapshot inspects snapshot.metrics (expects a dict) and snapshot.vs_previous / snapshot.vs_baseline (expects dicts or None) directly. If snapshot is a pycode-kg Snapshot the properties return typed dataclasses instead; we substitute a plain _BaseSnapshot carrying the raw dicts so the base implementation can serialise without modification.
